notes: sigma(y) = n! is solvable for every 3 <= n <= 250 (B38_2_main in NT/B38.2/B38_2_mathlib.lean: explicit y as a factor list of distinct primes certified by trial division, product of sigma(q^a) = n! checked by the kernel in 31 chunks, sigma_val for multiplicativity) and for 3 <= n <= 557 by exact computation (randomized exact cover of the exponents of n! by sigma(q^a) atoms with distinct q, Mersenne primes for the power of 2). Literature had n <= 28 (Alekseyev, A055486). Outside Lean: the range 251 <= n <= 557 (Python check with exact arithmetic and deterministic Miller-Rabin).

sources.cite: M. A. Alekseyev, J. Integer Seq. 19 (2016) 16.5.2; OEIS A055486

prior_art.note: Extension past n = 28 not found in the literature.
